questions.stem:
A uniform rod $AB$ has length $2a$ and mass $M$. The rod is held in equilibrium in a horizontal position by two vertical light strings which are attached to the rod at $C$ and $D$, where $AC = \frac{2}{5}a$ and $DB = \frac{3}{5}a$, as shown in Figure 1.

A particle $P$ is placed on the rod at $B$.

The rod remains horizontal and in equilibrium.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find, in terms of $M$, the largest possible mass of the particle $P$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M($D$): $\frac{3a}{5}Xg = \frac{2a}{5}Mg$ M1A1
(Other possible equations: ($\uparrow$) $T_D = Mg + Xg$; M($A$), $Mga + Xg \cdot 2a = T_D\frac{7a}{5}$; M($B$), $Mga = T_D\frac{3a}{5}$ ($T_D$ would then need to be eliminated); M($C$), $Mg\frac{3a}{5} + Xg\frac{8a}{5} = T_D a$; M($G$), $Xga = T_D\frac{2a}{5}$)
$X = \frac{2M}{3}$, 0.67M or better A1
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For an equation (or inequality) in X , M and a only (allow consistent missing a's) with correct no. of terms. Allow if one g is missing. N.B. M0 if $T_C$ appears and never becomes zero
- A1 Correct equation or inequality

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that the mass of $P$ is $\frac{1}{2}M$
(b) find, in terms of $M$ and $g$, the tension in the string that is attached to the rod at $C$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M($D$): $T_Ca + \frac{1}{2}Mg\frac{3a}{5} = \frac{2a}{5}Mg$ M1A1
(Other possible equations: ($\uparrow$) $T_C + T_D = Mg + \frac{1}{2}Mg$; M($A$), $Mga + \frac{1}{2}Mg \cdot 2a = T_C\frac{2a}{5} + T_D\frac{7a}{5}$; M($B$), $Mga = T_C\frac{8a}{5} + T_D\frac{3a}{5}$ ($T_D$ would need eliminating); M($C$), $Mg\frac{3a}{5} + \frac{1}{2}Mg\frac{8a}{5} = T_D a$; M($G$), $T_C\frac{3a}{5} + \frac{1}{2}Mga = T_D\frac{2a}{5}$)
$T_C = \frac{1}{10}Mg$ oe A1
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For an equation in $T_C$ , M , g and a only (allow consistent missing a's or if g('s) missing) with correct no. of terms. M0 if they assume that $T_C = T_D$ or if they assume their X value from (a).

questions.stem:
A rough plane is inclined to the horizontal at an angle $\alpha$, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$

A particle $P$ of mass 2 kg is held in equilibrium on the plane by a horizontal force of magnitude $X$ newtons, as shown in Figure 2. The force acts in a vertical plane which contains a line of greatest slope of the inclined plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that when $X = 14.7$ there is no frictional force acting on $P$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
($\nearrow$), $14.7\cos\alpha = 2g\sin\alpha + F$ (could be $-F$)
OR: ($\rightarrow$), $14.7 + F\cos\alpha = R\sin\alpha$ AND ($\uparrow$), $R\cos\alpha + F\sin\alpha = 2g$ AND eliminate $R$ to give an equation in $F$ only.
Verification methods: $14.7\cos\alpha = (11.76) = 2g\sin\alpha$ (i.e. verification that $X=14.7 \Rightarrow F=0$)
OR: $X\cos\alpha = 2g\sin\alpha \Rightarrow X = 14.7$ (i.e. verification that $F=0 \Rightarrow X=14.7$) M1 A1
so $F = 0^*$ oe A1*
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Equation in F only, correct no of terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion (M0 if they use F = 0.5R) N.B. Allow the equation without F. Allow use of m instead of 2 for the Mmark
- A1* cao Must state a conclusion or, if verifying, must state clearly $X = 14.7 \Rightarrow F = 0$ OR $F = 0 \Rightarrow X = 14.7$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The coefficient of friction between $P$ and the plane is 0.5
(b) Find the smallest possible value of $X$.
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
$F_1 = 0.5S$ B1
Two equations taken from:
($\nearrow$), $X\cos\alpha + F_1 = 2g\sin\alpha$
($\searrow$), $S = X\sin\alpha + 2g\cos\alpha$
($\rightarrow$), $X + F_1\cos\alpha = S\sin\alpha$
($\uparrow$), $S\cos\alpha + F_1\sin\alpha = 2g$
M1A2 M1A2 (N.B. M0 for both equations if they put $X=14.7$ anywhere)
$X = \frac{4g}{11}$, 3.6 or 3.56 or 3.57 A1
(N.B. Enter marks for the equations on ePen in the order in which they appear above.)
(8)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 $F_1 = 0.5S$ seen e.g. on a diagram (even if wrong direction)
- M1 A resolution, correct no of terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion. Allow use of m instead of 2 for the A mark. A2 Correct equation, -1 each error

questions.stem:
Two children, Alan and Bhavana, are standing on the horizontal floor of a lift, as shown in Figure 3.

The lift has mass 250 kg. The lift is raised vertically upwards with constant acceleration by a vertical cable which is attached to the top of the lift. The cable is modelled as being light and inextensible. While the lift is accelerating upwards, the tension in the cable is 3616 N.

As the lift accelerates upwards, the floor of the lift exerts a force of magnitude 565 N on Alan and a force of magnitude 226 N on Bhavana.

Air resistance is modelled as being negligible and Alan and Bhavana are modelled as particles.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) By considering the forces acting on the lift only, find the acceleration of the lift.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$3616 - 250g - 565 - 226 = 250a$ M1 A1
$a = 1.5\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ A1
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Equation in a only, correct no. of terms, condone sign errors

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
$565 - mg = m\times1.5$ M1A1ft
$m = 50\,(\mathrm{kg})$ A1
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Equation in m (mass of A) only, correct terms, condone sign errors. A1ft Correct equation ft on their a

questions.stem:
A small ball is projected vertically upwards with speed $29.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ from a point $A$ which is $19.6$ m above horizontal ground.

The ball is modelled as a particle moving freely under gravity until it hits the ground. It is assumed that the ball does not rebound.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the distance travelled by the ball while its speed is less than $14.7\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$0 = 14.7^2 - 2gs$ M1A1
$s = 22$ or $22.1$ (m) A1
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Complete method to find distance UP. N.B. They may find time UP (1.5s) AND use it to find distance UP OR: (Distance from A to top – Distance from '14.7' to top) = (44.1 – 33.075)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the time for which the ball is moving with a speed of more than $29.4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
$19.6 = 29.4t + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ M1A1
(N.B. $19.6 = 29.4t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ is M0A0; $-19.6 = 29.4t + \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ is M0A0; $-19.6 = 29.4t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ is M0A0 unless they go on to subtract 6 from the positive root)
$t = 0.61$ or $0.606$ (s) A1
(3)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Complete method to find required time. N.B. They may find the speed as it hits the ground ($g\sqrt{13} = 35.334...$) AND use it to find the time.
- A1 cao N.B. If they add to or subtract from 0.606, it's M0 for an incorrect method.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Sketch a speed-time graph for the motion of the ball from the instant when it is projected from $A$ to the instant when it hits the ground. Show clearly where your graph meets the axes.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1 shape: V shape with $v$ coord of end point $> 29.4$ and each half roughly equally inclined to the $t$-axis. B0 if a vertical line is included at the end.
B1 29.4 independent
B1 3 independent
(3)

questions.stem:
[In this question, $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors.]

A particle $A$ of mass 0.5 kg is at rest on a smooth horizontal plane.

At time $t=0$, two forces, $\mathbf{F}_1 = (-3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})$ N and $\mathbf{F}_2 = (p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j})$ N, where $p$ and $q$ are constants, are applied to $A$.

Given that $A$ moves in the direction of the vector $(\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j})$,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
$(-3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j})+(p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j}) = (-3+p)\mathbf{i}+(2+q)\mathbf{j}$ M1
$\frac{(-3+p)}{(2+q)} = \frac{1}{-2}$ M1A1
$2p+q-4=0^*$ Allow $0=2p+q-4$ but nothing else A1*
(4)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 For adding and collecting i's and j's. N.B. Could be implied by p = 4 and q = -4
- M1 Using ratios oe to set up an equation in p and q only, allow the ratio the wrong way round. M0 if they write down: $-3+p=1$ and $2+q=-2$ and NEVER use ratios, but ignore these equations if they go on to use ratios

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $p=5$
(b) find the speed of $A$ at time $t=4$ seconds.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
$p=5 \Rightarrow q=-6 \Rightarrow$ Resultant force $= (2\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j})$ B1
$(2\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}) = 0.5\mathbf{a}$ M1
$\mathbf{v} = (4\mathbf{i}-8\mathbf{j})\times 4$ M1
Speed $= \sqrt{16^2+(-32)^2} = \sqrt{1280} = 16\sqrt{5} = 36\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ or better M1A1
(5)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Use of F = ma where F is their resultant (must have attempted to add the two forces) (M0 if they include g)
- M1 Use of v = at with t = 4 where a is their acceleration. (M0 if u is non-zero)
- M1 Use of Pythagoras to find magnitude of v OR a OR F, including square root. N.B. The above 3 steps may appear in any order but must be entered on ePen in the order as above.
- A1 Any equivalent surd or correct to at least 2 SF

questions.stem:
A particle $P$ of mass $m$ is attached to one end of a light inextensible string. Another particle $Q$, also of mass $m$, is attached to the other end of the string. The string passes over a small smooth pulley which is fixed at the edge of a rough horizontal table. Particle $Q$ is held at rest on the table and particle $P$ hangs vertically below the pulley with the string taut, as shown in Figure 4.

The pulley, $P$ and $Q$ all lie in the same vertical plane.

The coefficient of friction between $Q$ and the table is $\mu$, where $\mu < 1$

Particle $Q$ is released from rest.

The tension in the string before $Q$ hits the pulley is $kmg$, where $k$ is a constant.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
$F = \mu mg$ B1
For $P$: $mg - kmg = ma$ Allow $mg-T=ma$ M1A1
For $Q$: $kmg - F = ma$ Allow $T-F=ma$ M1A1
(Either of these may be replaced by: $mg - F = 2ma$ (whole system))
Produce an equation in $k$ and $\mu$ only using $T=kmg$ M1
$k = \frac{1}{2}(1+\mu)$ A1
(7)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 for $F = \mu mg$ seen e.g. on a diagram
- M1 Equation of motion for P (and for Q) with correct no. of terms, condone sign errors. A1 Correct equation (allow -a) N.B. (-a) must be used in both equations
- A1 oe Must appear in (a)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Given that $Q$ is initially a distance $d$ from the pulley,
(b) find, in terms of $d$, $g$ and $\mu$, the time taken by $Q$, after release, to reach the pulley.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Attempt to find the acceleration. M1
[Note that some possible correct forms are: $a = \frac{1}{2}g(1-\mu)$ or $g(1-k)$ or $g(k-\mu)$]
$d = \frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{2}g(1-\mu)t^2$ M1A1
$t = \sqrt{\dfrac{4d}{g(1-\mu)}}$ A1
(4)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Attempt to find the acceleration in terms of g and $\mu$ or g and k or g, k and $\mu$
- M1 Complete method to find an equation in d, g, t and $\mu$ only, condone a sign error. A1 Correct equation in d, g, t and $\mu$ only
- A1 Any equivalent form

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Describe what would happen if $\mu \geqslant 1$, giving a reason for your answer.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
$P$ or $Q$ (or the system) would not move B1
Accept any of $T=mg$, $T>mg$, $T\geqslant mg$, $a=0$, $a<0$, $a\leqslant 0$, $F=T$, $F>T$, $F\geqslant T$, $F>mg$. Allow $F$ replaced by $\mu R$
N.B. Forces referred to must be clearly defined so e.g. use of vague terms like 'forward force', 'opposite force', 'force to the left or right' is B0. DB1
(2)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1 Correct statement. B0 if incorrect extras. DB1 Correct reason

questions.stem:
[In this question, $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are horizontal unit vectors directed due east and due north respectively and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

Two ships, $A$ and $B$, are moving with constant velocities.
The velocity of $A$ is $(3\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ and the velocity of $B$ is $(p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
$\sqrt{3^2+12^2}$ M1
$\sqrt{153}$, $3\sqrt{17}$, 12 or better ($\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$) A1
(2)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Use of Pythagoras with square root

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The ships are modelled as particles.
At 12 noon, $A$ is at the point with position vector $(-9\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})$ km and $B$ is at the point with position vector $(16\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})$ km.
At time $t$ hours after 12 noon,
$$\overrightarrow{AB} = \left[(25-12t)\mathbf{i} - 9t\mathbf{j}\right]\,\mathrm{km}$$
(b) Find the value of $p$ and the value of $q$.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
(Allow column vectors throughout)
$(-9\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})+t(3\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})$ M1A1
$(16\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})+t(p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j})$ A1
$\overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} = (16\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})+t(p\mathbf{i}+q\mathbf{j}) - \left[(-9\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j})+t(3\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j})\right]$ M1A1
$= \left[25+t(p-3)\right]\mathbf{i} + t(q-12)\mathbf{j}$
Compare with: $\left[(25-12t)\mathbf{i} - 9t\mathbf{j}\right]$ or e.g. use $\mathbf{b} = \overrightarrow{AB}+\mathbf{a}$ to obtain an equation in $p$ only and an equation in $q$ only. May be implied by correct answers only.
($-12 = p-3$ and $-9 = q-12$)
(N.B. This mark may not be available if they go wrong and the $t$'s don't cancel.) M1
$p=-9$, $q=3$ A1
(7)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Correct structure for either
- M1 Allow a − b. A1 for a correct unsimplified expression for either b – a or a – b

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the bearing of $A$ from $B$ when the ships are 15 km apart, giving your answer to the nearest degree.
(7)
parts.mark_scheme:
$(25-12t)^2+(-9t)^2 = 15^2$ ($225t^2-600t+400=0$) M1A1
$t = \frac{4}{3}$ A1
$\pm(9\mathbf{i}-12\mathbf{j})$ Note that this is a method mark. DM1
$\tan\theta = \frac{9}{12}$ M1
$\theta = 37^\circ$ A1
Bearing is $323^\circ$ to nearest degree A1
(7)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1 Use of Pythagoras to give an equation in t only. Allow with a square root.
- A1 t = 1.3 or better
- DM1 Use of their t to find $\overrightarrow{AB}$ or $\overrightarrow{BA}$, dependent on previous M. May be implied. Allow if they use one of their two incorrect t values.
- M1 For an equation in a relevant angle for their AB. Could be implied by a relevant angle seen on a diagram which could need checking with a calculator
- A1 Correct relevant angle e.g $37^\circ, 53^\circ, 127^\circ$, etc or better
